confidence_notes: Meal, beer and coffee anchors rest on Boston-specific aggregates seen in web search result summaries (Numbeo-credited figures via Expatica and combien-coute, plus Wise, MyLifeElsewhere, Where and When). I did not open the underlying pages, and the data is crowd-sourced. Cocktail ($15-18 across sources; Expatistan's $18 uses few data points) is moderately supported. No Boston-specific wine-by-the-glass average was found, so wine is inferred from national and other-city reports (about $14-16+ per glass) and a ~1.9x relationship to the ~$8 beer. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July peak season (no accommodation searches or live listings checked); Boston's small hostel supply and possible event-driven July demand make them the least certain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink use Boston-specific aggregate figures. Accommodation is judged by analogy to other high-cost US Northeast urban markets such as New York and Washington DC, adjusted for Boston's limited hostel supply and strong July peak-season hotel demand.
